review_notes: I read the whole file (lines 1–116) and grepped the MarkovProcess tree for downstream uses of these declarations. The only use outside this file is CanonicalDiscreteLaw.lean. It uses `DiscretePath.coordinate n` unapplied, inside `.map (...)`, and uses `measurable_coordinate`. The simp interface is small and coherent. `coordinate_apply` and `coordinateProcess_apply` are `rfl` lemmas oriented from the definition to `ω n`. They rewrite in the right direction, do not compete, and cannot cycle. `canonicalFiltration_apply` is not `@[simp]`, and I think that is correct. Its right-hand side is a `⨆ k ≤ n, comap …` expression, which would expand the filtration in every goal that mentions it. The unapplied forms (`coordinate n`, `coordinateProcess n`) have no unfolding simp lemma. A lemma such as `coordinateProcess n = coordinate n` would be possible, but I found no use that needs it, and the downstream code uses `coordinate` directly, so I don't think it is justified. I did not run Lean, so I can't rule out simp-set interactions in files I didn't read.
